cases.prompt: Use the site-structure-optimizer skill in linking mode for mailcraft.example, a small SaaS blog. No crawler connector, WebFetch, WebSearch or curl is available in this session, so work only from the two files, which are a Screaming Frog export from 2026-10-12. `pages.csv` is the full page inventory (12 indexable pages). `inlinks.csv` lists every internal link as one row per unique source-to-destination pair; the sitewide header and footer links are listed once, from the home page, and the Link position column says whether a link is Header, Footer or Content (contextual). The five important pages are the home page, /guides/email-marketing/, /guides/email-marketing/automation/, /tools/subject-line-tester/ and /pricing/. There is no traffic data. Treat every link target as resolving; do not try to fetch anything. You already have my approval to save the report to `seo-reports/site-structure-optimizer/2026-10-13-mailcraft.md`. Give me the diagnosis and the link plan in chat as well.

assertions.label: structure score 100 - 20 (2 orphans) - 5 (/about/ has no contextual inbound link) - 10 (1.6 links per page is below every model's range)
chat answer carries the same score

criteria: Exactly two orphans are listed (black-friday-email-ideas-2024 and welcome-series-examples) and no other page is called an orphan; each orphan either gets a disposition (keep and link, noindex, or redirect) with a reason, or, because its traffic value is unknown, is put to the user as a numbered choice between those options

The score arithmetic is shown as deductions from 100 that sum to 65: -20 for two orphans, -5 for /about/ having no inbound contextual link, -10 for average links per page (19 links / 12 pages, about 1.6) being outside the chosen model's target range; no important page is charged for being deeper than 3 clicks

The anchor analysis flags 'email marketing guide' (4 links to the pillar) as a repeated exact-match anchor to one target and 'click here' from the deliverability checklist as a generic anchor to rewrite
The link plan is a table of source, target and anchor rows with at least three rows that give the two orphans inbound contextual links from topically related pages
The answer does not claim to have crawled, fetched or curl-checked anything, and link counts are labeled User-provided rather than Measured

cases.prompt: Use the site-structure-optimizer skill in architecture mode. We are rebuilding the marketing site for Ledgerly, a SaaS accounting tool for freelancers (about 30 pages at launch). Goals: free-trial signups, organic traffic to the guides, and a clean docs area. Pages we will have: home, product overview, three feature pages (invoicing, expenses, tax estimates), pricing, integrations, about, contact, a blog with roughly 15 posts about freelancer taxes and bookkeeping, and a 6-page docs section. The five most important pages are home, pricing, the invoicing feature page, the tax-estimates feature page and a pillar guide on freelancer taxes. Two legacy URLs are still linked from partner sites and must keep resolving, so if you change them they need 301 redirects: /blog/2024/05/launch-announcement/ and /features.html; we want clean URL patterns, not grandfathered exceptions. No crawler data, no web access; work from this description only and do not fetch anything. Do not save a report; give me everything in chat.

assertions.label: nothing saved when told not to

criteria: An ASCII hierarchy tree is shown with a URL or URL pattern at every node (unnamed blog posts or docs articles may be grouped under one node that shows their URL pattern), and none of the five important pages sits deeper than 3 clicks from home
The URL map is a table with page, URL, parent, navigation location and priority columns, and it flags the dated blog URL pattern (/blog/2024/05/...) and the .html extension as mistakes to fix
A redirect map lists both existing URLs with their new destination and a 301, and the architecture score arithmetic shows each deduction (or states that there are none) and sums correctly
The header navigation spec has between 4 and 7 items with the free-trial CTA rightmost, and the footer and breadcrumb rules are stated
The hub/spoke plan names the freelancer-taxes pillar as a hub with specific blog posts as spokes, with cross-section links between features and guides
The handoff recommends running linking mode next, and the answer does not claim to have crawled or fetched anything

cases.prompt: Use the site-structure-optimizer skill in architecture mode for Peakline Roofing, a local roofing contractor whose site is being rebuilt. The statement of work is in `sow.md` in this folder; read it for the page cap. No crawler, Figma MCP, web access or traffic data is available; work from this list and do not fetch anything. Pages the client wants: home, about, contact, privacy policy, terms and conditions, 404, blog archive, 6 blog posts, and these service and company pages: roof repair, roof replacement, storm damage repair, gutter installation, gutter repair, skylight installation, commercial roofing, financing, reviews, service areas, our process, careers. The five most important pages are home, roof repair, roof replacement, storm damage repair and contact. Do not save a report; give me everything in chat, including the three Mermaid boards.

assertions.label: nothing saved when told not to
final countable count equals the cap of 8 (13 requested countable pages incl. about, 5 merged or deferred)

criteria: The SOW sentence stating the 8-page cap is quoted, and home, contact, privacy policy, terms and conditions, 404, the blog archive and the blog posts are shown in the sitemap but explicitly not counted toward the cap

Exactly 8 countable pages remain in the final sitemap; the other 5 requested countable pages (about counts as one of the 13) are each either merged into a named page or deferred to a Phase 2 list with a reason, and none of the five important pages is merged or deferred

Three separate Mermaid diagrams are given, each starting with graph TD: a site map in which the home page, Level 1 pages and deeper pages use different node shapes (and classDef font sizes), a main navigation board containing only header items with the CTA rightmost, and a footer board containing only footer pages grouped into columns

A decision table lists every requested page with an action (keep, revise, merge, retire, create or defer) and a reason; scores are N/A or Estimated because no traffic data exists, and the answer never claims to have fetched, crawled or opened Figma
The architecture score arithmetic is shown and the handoff recommends running linking mode next
